summary:
Tonitrus Luna – Lunar Landing Site Navigator

Tonitrus Luna is an interactive lunar mission planning platform designed to identify and evaluate suitable landing sites near the Moon’s South Pole. Our project addresses the challenges of lunar exploration by combining scientific data, visualization, and mission-planning tools in one integrated platform. It features a 3D lunar globe, solar illumination analysis, landing site comparison, and a horizon radar to evaluate sunlight availability and terrain obstructions. It also calculates potential solar power generation, Earth visibility, and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows using lunar libration data. Additionally, it integrates with space-tracking applications such as Celestia and Orbitrack, providing downloadable mission data for further analysis. This project is important because selecting a safe and sustainable lunar landing site is essential for future human exploration. By helping assess power availability, communication reliability, and environmental conditions, Tonitrus Luna supports better-informed decisions for future lunar missions, including Artemis.
details:
1. What does it do & how does it work?

Tonitrus Luna is an interactive mission planning tool that models extreme solar illumination and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication constraints at the Moon’s South Pole:

  • Topocentric Astronomical Engine: Computes real-time Sun and Earth positions using Meeus algorithms and JPL ephemerides, calculating topocentric azimuth and elevation for any lunar coordinate.
  • Grazing Sunlight & Solar Power: Sunlight at the poles grazes the horizon between −1.54∘-1.54^\circ−1.54∘ and +1.54∘+1.54^\circ+1.54∘. The tool models solar flux (W/m2W/m^2W/m2) and proves why vertical solar arrays capture up to 12×12\times12× more energy than horizontal panels, estimating power output for a 10 m210\text{ m}^210 m2 GaAs array (3.8 kW3.8\text{ kW}3.8 kW peak).
  • Libration & DTE Communication Windows: Models Earth’s ±7.9∘\pm 7.9^\circ±7.9∘ longitude and ±6.7∘\pm 6.7^\circ±6.7∘ latitude libration cycle, predicting when Earth dips behind crater rims to trigger communication blackouts.
  • LOLA Terrain Obstruction: Incorporates 360∘360^\circ360∘ elevation masks from NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter data for candidate Artemis landing sites (Shackleton, Malapert, Nobile, Chandrayaan-3, IM-1 Odysseus, etc.).
  • Interactive Visuals: Features a 360° Polar Horizon Radar with a −5∘-5^\circ−5∘ dip ring, a scrubbable dual-axis ephemeris timeline (1×1\times1× to 1,500×1,500\times1,500× speed), and an interactive 3D lunar globe with dynamic terminator shadows.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Replaces Complex Tools: Eliminates the steep learning curve of fragmented SPICE command-line tools with a unified, zero-install web interface.
  • Instant Site Trade Studies: Side-by-side Landing Sites Comparator evaluates illumination %, longest continuous darkness, and DTE availability in seconds.
  • Mission Risk Reduction: Helps mission planners choose launch and landing epochs that maximize solar power and prevent communication loss.
  • Zero-Install Portability: Runs completely offline in any modern browser on desktop or mobile.

3. What is the intended impact?

  • Artemis & Commercial Lunar Missions: Assists mission design for NASA Artemis III, international agencies (ESA, ISRO, JAXA), and commercial CLPS landers (Intuitive Machines, Astrobotic).
  • STEM & Higher Education: Demystifies complex orbital mechanics (librations, anomalistic months, polar grazing geometry) for university classrooms and museums.
  • Public Engagement: Connects surface mission design directly with ground-based amateur astronomy.

4. What tools, languages, and software were used?

  • AI Architecture: Google Antigravity (ephemeris formulation, code generation, UI engineering, and automated browser testing).
  • Languages & Web Stack: JavaScript (ES6+) for zero-dependency astronomical math; HTML5 Canvas 2D for custom vector rendering of radar, timeline, and 3D globe; CSS3 for a space-grade dark glassmorphism design system.
  • Scientific Data: NASA LOLA topographic profiles, Jean Meeus astronomical algorithms, and NASA/ISRO/CNSA mission archives.
  • Hosting & Packaging: Netlify for global CDN deployment; PowerShell for POSIX-compliant forward-slash ZIP packaging and single-file bundling.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Celestial Synergy Hub: Cross-platform interoperability bridging surface planning with 4 popular space tracking tools:
    • Celestia: Exports .ssc Solar System Catalogs and .cel camera fly-to scripts.
    • Orbitrack: Exports .csv target databases and cislunar orbital elements.
    • ISS Detector & Star Walk: Generates standard 69-character NORAD TLEs for lunar orbiters (LRO, CAPSTONE, Gateway) and real-time Earth observer pointing coordinates (RA/Dec, Az/El) for Augmented Reality (AR) night-sky spotting.
    • CCSDS OEM XML: Exports standardized inter-agency navigation ephemerides.
  • Self-Contained Architecture: Entire app runs from a single 171 KB HTML file (tonitrusluna.html) with zero external network requests.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Extreme Lunar Polar Physics: Grazing sunlight angles (±1.54∘\pm 1.54^\circ±1.54∘), 27.3-day libration cycles, and cryogenic cold traps (<40 K<40\text{ K}<40 K).
  • Crater Topography: NASA LOLA elevation profiles to determine whether towering mountain peaks (e.g., Malapert Mons at +5,000 m+5,000\text{ m}+5,000 m) shield or block the Sun and Earth.
  • Human Factors & Telemetry: Color-coded status alerts (Green Optimal, Yellow Grazing, Red Blackout) and quick-jump date presets (Solstices, Artemis III, Chandrayaan-3, IM-1).
  • Comprehensive Lunar History: Curated a database of 50+ lunar missions (1959–2026+) documenting launch dates, power systems, communications bands, rover wheel mechanics, science instruments, and mission milestones.
